method: eval/raw/customer_latency_2026-10-14/measure.py method (CUST-MEENA, fresh visitor per call, 15-message pool cycled, same order, parallelism 1) against a local server (serve.py), vertex backend, Model Armor ON (taal-chat) in both runs. FIRST 24 of the 50 calls only: the $1.60 cap allowed ~24 turns per run (about $0.032 per turn). Same 24 prompts in the same order.
model: gemini-3.5-flash on every call in both runs (usage_metadata/model_version logged; both runs valid)
notes: Change 1 (stock prefetch) did not fire in the 24-call set: CUST-MEENA has no pending offer in the base tenant, so no offered SKU exists. It is exercised only in judge_path_after.json (Ravi after Approve on Tea), which has no BEFORE twin because the budget was spent.

Behaviour difference seen: with minimal thinking the model answered 'do you have quinoa?' and 'do you have kaju katli?' with three parallel get_stock calls (a text reply) instead of list_products (list picker) in 3 of 24 turns (quinoa twice, kaju katli once); in the BEFORE run those turns used list_products. Both are allowed by the prompt.

One run each, different minutes; model latency varies run to run, so treat a gain of under a second at p50 as noise. The p95/max gap (8.4 s vs 4.4 s) is mostly the long tail in the BEFORE run (turn 3 'what tea', 3 model calls, 8.8 s).
